title: Privilege topology and contextual scope encoding for RBAC v2
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Objective: Design a role model for RBAC v2 that encodes resource topology and contextual scopes to enable precise least-privilege, explainable permission checks, and reliable audit trails. The design must support multi-tenant resource hierarchies, temporal elevations, SSO/SAML group->role mappings, and a migration path from RBAC v1 while minimizing runtime evaluation overhead.

Key goals:
- Canonical resource hierarchy model (resource types, resource instances, ambient tenants, and attachment points).
- Contextual scope encoding: compact scope tokens that carry resource ancestry + conditional attributes (region, environment, retention-class) to allow fast membership checks and cacheable allow/deny results.
- Permission matrix: canonical verbs (read/write/admin/list) + fine-grained actions (invoke, rollout, manage-billing) with a deterministic resolution order.
- Deterministic deny precedence with explainable traces for every decision; include audit hooks that emit both the assertion inputs and the trace (policy matches, inherited grants, overrides).
- SSO/SAML mapping guidelines: preferred transformation rules for groups->roles, attribute-based claims mapping, inbound SAML assertion validation and role provisioning.
- Admin guardrails: breakglass account model, emergency elevation with TTL, approval workflow hooks, and tamper-evident audit entries.

Proposed model (summary):
- Resource Tree: each resource has a compact path string resource_path = <tenant>/<product>/<resource_type>/<resource_id>. Resource types declare allowable child types and cardinality.
- Scope Token: a signed, short-lived scope token contains {resource_path_prefixes, allowed_verbs, attributes, expiry, origin}. Tokens are created for service-to-service flows and can be cached at the proxy layer.
- RoleSets: roles map to permission tuples (resource_selector, allowed_verbs, constraints). RoleSets can include inline deny rules and attribute predicates.
- Evaluation flow: 1) collect principal roles (SSO groups, direct bindings, ephemeral elevations), 2) evaluate explicit denies, 3) evaluate allows by specificity (exact resource > prefix > global), 4) apply attribute predicates, 5) produce allow/deny + trace.

Non-goals:
- Not implementing an ABAC engine now; predicates will be expression-limited (simple equality, membership, and numeric ranges) to preserve cacheability and performance.
- Not replacing existing RBAC v1 bindings immediately — we will provide a compatibility shim and conversion tooling.

Migration plan (high-level):
- Phase 1: Schema additions (roleset table, role_bindings, scope_signing_keys). Backfill tools to translate RBAC v1 role->roleset mappings. DB migrations scrubs: add roleset_id to bindings, do not delete v1 columns.
- Phase 2: API compatibility layer: allow v1 tokens to be evaluated by the RBAC v2 engine; log mismatches and rare code paths.
- Phase 3: Opt-in tenants for RBAC v2, run canary on internal teams, collect policy coverage metrics, iterate predicates.

Observability & audit hooks:
- Every decision must emit an audit event containing: principal, roleset_ids considered, resource_path, action, evaluation_trace, resolved_grant, timestamp, request_id.
- Store a compact binary trace in the audit store and an indexed summary in BigQuery/Redwood analytics for long-term queries.
- Add tracing correlation to console: when an admin views a denied request, show the trace and the minimal change required to allow the request.

SSO/SAML mapping guidance:
- Prefer attribute-based mapping (eduPersonScopedAffiliation-like) for group->role derivation. For enterprise SAML, map SAML groups to RoleSet bindings rather than individual roles to reduce churn.
- Documented fallback: if SAML groups are stale, use an internal mapping table and emit telemetry whenever a mapping is used.

Security considerations:
- Signed scope tokens must be rotated using KMS; scope tokens are short-lived (<= 1h) except for long-lived service accounts which must use key-wrapped refresh tokens and stronger audit.
- Role provisioning changes (create/delete role) require 2-person approval for roles that include admin verbs.
- Provide audit-only mode for new role changes for 7 days before enforcement for high-risk tenants.

Deliverables:
- Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SEC/pages/RBAC-v2-privilege-topology (link placeholder)
- Migration scripts: gh-PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/1245 (schema), /pull/1256 (shims)
- RBAC v2 runtime: pkg/authz/roleset.go, pkg/authz/evaluator.go (implementation plan in repo)

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Predicate expressiveness vs cacheability: allowing full boolean expressions increases flexibility but will blow up cache invalidation. Prefer narrow predicates today with a plan to add a sandboxed predicate engine later.
- Representation of 'implicit parents' (e.g., org level capabilities that implicitly grant dataset-level capabilities) — do we expand bindings to explicit prefixes or rely on prefix checks at eval time? Current leaning: keep prefix checks at eval time for storage savings and clearer audit.
